messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert: rollout 'sdk-client-v2.1.0' showing spike in 5xx on paging endpoints (/v1/paging/generate). 18% 5xx over 3m, increased retries.

oncall-bot: @maya you're oncall for infra, can you take a look?

maya: looking now. seeing a lot of streaming handshake failures paired with invalid paging tokens. logs show 'unsupported frame' from client and proto deserial errors.

samir: which layer? gateway or runtime? could be framing change in sdk.

maya: gateway first. stack: gateway-proxy -> gateway-filter -> runtime. samples point to client sdk/2.1.0.

jordan: CS reports one paying customer seeing truncated pages and 502s. ticket #12345.

liam: traffic pattern: canary targets 12% of traffic. if clients pinned to canary id they'll keep hitting it. we should consider kill-switch + rollback.

maya: P1. I'm toggling the canary feature flag to stop new canary assignments.

maya: /ff toggle sdk_canary_v2 --off  (executed)

deploy-bot: Feature flag sdk_canary_v2 toggled OFF by maya at 2026-03-15T20:59:34Z :white_check_mark:

maya: monitoring now. error rate dropped to ~6% within 60s but still some stuck connections.

ops-eng: killing the flag prevents new canary but existing canary instances still serve pinned clients. propose rollback of canary artifacts.

samir: agree. likely cause: wire format tweak in v2.1.0 streaming framing. need both rollback and SDK patch.

support-tilly: reached out to affected_customer@example.com, advised temporary revert to sdk v2.0.x. they confirm partial recovery after client rollback.

maya: logs excerpt:
```text
gateway 2026-03-15T20:58:12Z ERROR handshake: unsupported frame from client sdk/2.1.0
runtime 2026-03-15T20:58:13Z WARN paging: token parse failed: invalid length
```

jordan: definitely looks like a client-side framing/encoding mismatch. paging endpoints use streaming frames for long results; if frame boundaries changed the runtime rejects them.

liam: initiating rollback: /deploy rollback canary-2026-03-15-20:50 -> starting now.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by liam for canary-2026-03-15-20:50. ETA ~120s. :gear:

maya: I'll stay on until rollback completes and error rates are back to baseline.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed at 2026-03-15T21:02:44Z. Canary instances replaced with previous stable build.

maya: observed metrics: 5xx down to 0.6% within 3m post-rollback. latency normalized.

samir: immediate mitigation confirmed. Next: revert the SDK change, publish 2.1.1 with compatibility shim and stricter e2e tests.

jordan: customer impact: one enterprise customer saw truncated pages and 502s for ~12 minutes; no data corruption. CS escalated; account manager looped in.

support-tilly: incident logged to CS tracker INC-20260315-43; customer PM notified.

maya: short post-incident actions: 1) patch SDK 2.1.1 with backward-compatible framing, 2) add integration test for streaming/paging on canary, 3) update rollout playbook to auto-kill flag if 5xx > 5% for 2m.

liam: I'll file the rollback runbook notes and add rollback checklist to console.

samir: owning SDK patch & release. ETA 24-48h, will run extended canary in staging with customers who opt-in.

jordan: I'll own monitoring and playbook changes; add an alert that correlates sdk-user-agent with 5xx on paging endpoints.

maya: handing off monitoring to night oncall @ops-night. If error rate >1% reopen incident as P0.

ops-night: ack, will monitor dashboards and escalate to maya if any regression.

deploy-bot: Incident mitigated by maya at 2026-03-15T21:12:04Z. Closing thread but keeping incident page open for postmortem actions.

maya: thanks all. please add any timeline details to the postmortem doc. we'll schedule a blameless review tomorrow.
